title: Gemini Omni Flash guide
claims: Extension appends to the end only and uses the last 10 seconds of the input as context; each turn adds 3 to 10 seconds, up to 30 seconds total.
If a character appeared only before the last 10 seconds, name it again or pass it as a reference image.
First and last frame interpolation takes two images and 3 to 10 seconds; image-to-video uses one image.
Multi-turn edits build on the previous result; adding 'keep everything else the same' preserves the rest of the scene.
Up to 3 reference images per character for up to 2 characters, 6 images in total.
Say 'single continuous shot' or 'no scene cuts' to avoid unwanted cuts.
notes: Last 2260 characters of the page were not read.

title: Edit videos & build scenes in Flow
claims: Extending a clip: choose a duration, describe how the action continues, add up to 3 image references for consistency.
A paused frame can be saved as an image and reused as an ingredient, start frame or end frame.
Scenebuilder arranges, reorders and trims whole clips with handles; it does not edit inside a clip.
Edits keep earlier versions in a History panel, and the original is not overwritten.

title: A Guide to Kling Turbo Start End Frame
claims: Keep lighting consistent across the start and end frames; a sharp lighting jump can cause flicker.
Avoid large perspective changes between the two frames, e.g. wide-angle start with telephoto end.
The end frame should show a related but different state with the same subject identity.
Five second clips transition more cleanly; ten seconds suits dramatic changes.
The start frame also sets the aspect ratio of the whole video.
notes: Reseller blog; the page does not cover chaining.

title: Google Flow SceneBuilder vs Luma Scenes
claims: Luma Scenes generates all keyframes together in one context and shows a storyboard for review before rendering video.
One keyframe can be regenerated without touching approved ones.
Flow SceneBuilder assembles separately generated clips and relies on character ingredients and extension for continuity.
notes: Written by a competitor; treat the comparison as marketing.

title: Veo 3 Video verlaengern (long video guide)
claims: Via the Gemini API each extension adds 7 seconds, up to 20 extensions, about 148 seconds in all (as the article states).
Drift is clothing colour, background and lighting shifting slightly between segments and adding up; check after every extension.
Repeat the full character description in every prompt; shortened descriptions let long hair become short.
Trim one or two overlapping frames at each join.
Starting each extension from a clean reference still reduces drift.
notes: Numbers are for the older Veo 3 API; the article does not measure degradation.

title: Kling V3: The Essentials
claims: End image works only in the single-scene Standard Prompt workflow, not with Multi-Prompting.
Multi-Prompt builds up to five shots in one generation, each with its own prompt and duration; the main prompt box must stay empty.
An Element needs an extra reference image besides the start image or it errors.
notes: Platform help page, not Kling itself.

title: Wan2.1-FLF2V-14B-720P model card
claims: The first-last-frame model outputs 720P only; the aspect ratio follows the input images.
It takes a first and a last image plus a prompt describing style, motion, background and camera.
Chinese prompts work better because training captions were mainly Chinese.

title: AniDoc: Animation Creation Made Easier
claims: Given a character image plus start and end sketches, it generates a temporally consistent in-between animation.
Correspondence matching keeps it robust when the pose differs between the reference and a frame.
notes: Abstract only; line-art workflow, only loosely related.

title: My Sora2 Workflow for Continuous Video Generation
claims: Loop: extract the last frame, write the next scene prompt from that frame plus the earlier context, generate, stitch.
The author calls the last-frame handoff what keeps continuity 'surprisingly stable'.
An optional reference image anchors the look from the start; deciding when to hold a shot versus add a beat is left open.

title: LTX 2.3 first, middle and last frame in ComfyUI
claims: Keyframes can sit at first, middle (frame 24 of 49) and last (frame 48) positions.
Frame count must be 8n+1 and reference images must match the target size, divisible by 32.
Add Guide is soft and lets motion flow; Inplace locks the frame nearly exactly but frees less motion.
Put a middle keyframe at the point where a transition happens.

title: How to Use LTX-2 for Keyframe Interpolation
claims: LTX-2 KeyframeInterpolationPipeline renders at half resolution then upsamples 2x with a distilled LoRA.
Keyframe images are given with a weight each; the article does not state a keyframe limit.

title: How to use Keyframes
claims: A keyframe sets the start or end frame; a prompt can guide the transition between them.
Extend can take an image keyframe as the destination; extended videos run up to 9 seconds from a default 4 second clip.

title: LTXVAddGuide node
claims: Guide frame index must be a multiple of 8 for inputs of 9 or more frames; negative values count from the end.
Guide strength runs 0 to 10, default 1.0 (full conditioning).

title: ConsistI2V: Enhancing Visual Consistency for Image-to-Video Generation
claims: Attention spanning the first frame preserves subject, background and style; noise initialised from the first frame's low frequencies preserves layout.
The same ideas are applied to long auto-regressive generation; evaluation uses a new I2V-Bench.

title: Captain Cinema: Towards Short Movie Generation
claims: Stage one plans keyframes for the whole story to hold scenes and characters consistent; stage two generates motion between them.
Authors claim narrative-consistent short movies; no numbers in the abstract.

title: Runway Gen-4 References: a creator workflow
claims: Use a simple scene reference with clean walls and low clutter; busy scenes can melt or warp.
Change only one variable per shot (location, camera or time of day) so drift can be traced.
Change location by swapping the Scene reference while keeping the character reference.

title: How to Use Kling 3.0 Pro
claims: Multi-shot: each shot 1 to 15 seconds in one multi_prompt call; total is the sum of the shots.
end_image_url sets a target final frame; suggested uses are morphs, camera moves to a fixed frame, loops and connecting two scenes.
Elements (tagged @Element1...) hold characters or objects across multi-shot sequences.
The author's testing: clips of 3 to 6 seconds keep motion tighter; longer clips drift more.

title: Kling 3.0 Turbo guide
claims: Multi-shot syntax is a shot number, seconds and a prompt per shot; one to six shots, each at least 1 second.
Keep each shot prompt under about 500 characters and to a single beat.
Starting from a still fixes the look before motion begins.

title: LTX 2.5 First & Last Frame to Video
claims: Match aspect ratio, horizon and subject scale in both frames or the model warps geometry.
Describe both the opening beat and the end state in the prompt.
Very high guidance can overconstrain motion; lower it if motion looks stiff.

title: How to chain AI video clips into one shot without the hidden stutter
claims: Matched frames do not match velocity: clips ease to a stop, so chaining from the last frame restarts from rest and hitches.
Generate longer than needed (e.g. 5 to 6 s for 4 s) and take the chaining frame before the deceleration zone, often the last 10 to 15 percent.
Decide the seed frame for the next clip at planning time; the author says this cut re-chaining from four tries to one.

title: Why do the first frames of an AI-extended clip look wrong
claims: Extension regenerates frames around the join; the first two frames are often duplicated, smeared or off-model.
Start the new clip at frame three; a frame-only extension also loses character, location and camera context.
For long chains use reference-to-video with locked character and location references.

title: Stable Video Infinity: Infinite-Length Video Generation with Error Recycling
claims: Authors name the cause of drift as a train/test mismatch: clean training inputs but imperfect self-generated conditioning at test time.
Error-recycling fine-tuning feeds the model its own past errors; authors report state of the art on three benchmarks.

title: Error Analyses of Auto-Regressive Video Diffusion Models
claims: Two failure modes: history forgetting and temporal degradation.
More past frames in the context reduce forgetting (proved), and the two failures are strongly correlated in experiments.

title: TokenTrim: Inference-Time Token Pruning for Autoregressive Long Video Generation
claims: Authors argue drift comes from corrupted tokens reused as conditioning, not from low model capacity.
Removing unstable tokens from the context at inference improves long-horizon consistency (authors' claim).
notes: Abstract only; author names not read.

title: How to colour-match AI video clips
claims: Each generation is graded on its own, so five shots of one scene can come back with five palettes.
State colour temperature as a number (3200K, 6500K) and repeat one palette line in every prompt.
Generate the establishing wide first and use it as the reference for closer shots; grade in a dedicated pass before editing.

title: Pack and Force Your Memory: Long-form and Consistent Video Generation
claims: MemoryPack retrieves short and long term context using text and image as global guidance, aiming at minute-level consistency at linear cost.
Direct Forcing aligns training with inference to cut error propagation (authors' claim).

title: HiAR: hierarchical denoising for long autoregressive video
claims: Conditioning each block on context at the same noise level, not a fully clean one, is said to reduce error build-up.
On VBench with 20 second videos the authors report the lowest temporal drift among compared methods.
notes: Abstract only; title wording is a paraphrase.

title: Flowception
claims: Inserting and denoising frames in any order is said to reduce error build-up versus strictly autoregressive models.
The same process covers image-to-video and frame interpolation.

title: Test-Time Correction for distilled autoregressive video diffusion
claims: Test-Time Correction uses the first frame as a stable anchor to keep long generation consistent, with no training.
Authors report it matches training-based methods on 30 second benchmarks.
notes: Abstract only; title is a paraphrase.

title: Multi-shot video stitching API
claims: Scale all clips to one resolution, frame rate and aspect ratio before joining; mismatches show as stutter or letterboxing.
Concatenation does not fix continuity, it only places the mismatch back to back.
Use crossfades or wipes when shots clash; add captions after stitching.

title: The Transition Troubleshooter: Fixing Video Clip Gaps
claims: Extend clips slightly past the cut and use a short crossfade to mask small differences.
Reuse the same wording for fixed character details and make short clips, reviewing each before the next.

title: How to Fix Background Artifacts in AI Video
claims: Check a clip at normal speed and frame by frame; a repair can look clean when paused and jitter in playback.
Log the first and last frames where a defect appears and lock the approved parts before regenerating.

title: Kling AI video post-processing with FFmpeg
claims: The author says Kling colour balance can drift within a 5 to 10 second clip, about 5600K toward 5100K.
A deflicker filter normalises luminance across a window of frames.
notes: Colour numbers are one author's observation.
